words.enDefinition: one sentence stating the central point your essay proves

examples.en: My TA underlined my thesis statement and asked me to make it more specific.
examples.zh: 助教在我的「论点句」下面画了线，让我写得更具体一点。

examples.en: A strong thesis statement belongs at the end of your introduction paragraph.
examples.zh: 一个有力的「论点句」应该放在开头段的末尾。

words.enDefinition: an early version of the main claim you keep refining

examples.en: Bring a working thesis to the writing center so the tutor can react to it.
examples.zh: 带一个「暂定论点」去写作中心，让辅导老师给出反馈。

examples.en: My working thesis changed completely after I read two more journal articles.
examples.zh: 读完另外两篇期刊文章之后，我的「暂定论点」完全变了。

words.enDefinition: first sentence of a paragraph announcing its main point

examples.en: Each body paragraph should open with a clear topic sentence.
examples.zh: 每个主体段都应该以清晰的「主题句」开头。

examples.en: The tutor circled my topic sentence because it did not match the paragraph.
examples.zh: 辅导老师圈出了我的「主题句」，因为它和段落内容对不上。

words.enDefinition: a middle paragraph developing one point behind the thesis

examples.en: My essay needs three body paragraphs, one for each supporting point.
examples.zh: 我的文章需要三个「主体段」，每个论点各写一段。

examples.en: The TA said my second body paragraph was too thin and needed evidence.
examples.zh: 助教说我的第二个「主体段」太单薄，需要补充证据。

collocations: topic sentence of a body paragraph

words.enDefinition: an opening line designed to seize the reader's attention

examples.en: Start your essay with a hook, maybe a surprising statistic about sleep.
examples.zh: 文章开头用一个「引子」，比如一个关于睡眠的惊人数据。

examples.en: The tutor suggested replacing my question with a short anecdote as the hook.
examples.zh: 辅导老师建议把我的提问换成一个小故事来当「引子」。

words.enDefinition: a word or sentence connecting ideas between paragraphs

examples.en: Add a transition so paragraph two does not feel like a sudden jump.
examples.zh: 加一个「过渡」，第二段就不会显得太突兀。

examples.en: Good transitions guide the reader from one argument to the next.
examples.zh: 好的「过渡」能引导读者从一个论点走向下一个论点。

words.enDefinition: a small connector like however that links sentences

examples.en: Overusing transition words like moreover can make your essay sound mechanical.
examples.zh: 过度使用「过渡词」会让文章显得很机械。

examples.en: My professor circled every transition word and told me to vary them.
examples.zh: 教授圈出了每个「过渡词」，让我换着使用。

words.enDefinition: a phrase like in addition that bridges two ideas

examples.en: A transitional phrase like in addition keeps the two paragraphs connected.
examples.zh: 用 in addition 这样的「过渡短语」，两段就能自然衔接。

examples.en: The TA circled each transitional phrase and suggested smoother options.
examples.zh: 助教圈出每个「过渡短语」，建议了更自然的替换。

collocations: a transitional phrase like in addition
start the paragraph with a transitional phrase

words.enDefinition: the final sentence of a paragraph wrapping up its point

examples.en: End the paragraph with a concluding sentence that ties back to your thesis.
examples.zh: 段落结尾用一个「段落总结句」，呼应你的论点。

examples.en: My concluding sentence introduced a brand-new idea, which confused the reader.
examples.zh: 我的「段落总结句」引入了一个全新的想法，把读者搞糊涂了。

words.enDefinition: the final paragraph restating the argument and ending memorably

examples.en: In the closing paragraph, restate your thesis in fresh words.
examples.zh: 在「结尾段」里，用新的说法重申你的论点。

examples.en: The TA praised my closing paragraph for not simply repeating the introduction.
examples.zh: 助教称赞我的「结尾段」没有简单重复开头。

collocations: restate the thesis in the closing paragraph

words.enDefinition: the opening paragraph that presents the topic and thesis

examples.en: Your introduction paragraph should end with a clearly stated thesis.
examples.zh: 你的「开头段」应该以明确陈述的论点收尾。

examples.en: The tutor helped me restructure my introduction paragraph so it flowed better.
examples.zh: 辅导老师帮我调整了「开头段」的结构，读起来更流畅。

collocations: end the introduction paragraph with the thesis

words.enDefinition: a paragraph-by-paragraph plan made before drafting

examples.en: Sketch a quick essay outline before you start the actual writing.
examples.zh: 动笔之前，先快速列一个「文章提纲」。

examples.en: My essay outline has five sections, each with a note about evidence.
examples.zh: 我的「文章提纲」有五个部分，每部分都标了要用什么证据。

words.enDefinition: facts, quotes, and examples backing up each point

examples.en: Every claim in your essay needs supporting evidence from credible places.
examples.zh: 文章里的每个论点都需要可靠来源的「支撑论据」。

examples.en: The TA flagged a paragraph where my opinion had no supporting evidence.
examples.zh: 助教标记了我只有观点、没有任何「支撑论据」的一段。

words.enDefinition: a specific fact or example that fleshes out a point

examples.en: Add one supporting detail to each claim so the paragraphs feel concrete.
examples.zh: 每个论点下补一条「支撑细节」，段落才显得具体。

examples.en: My supporting details were too vague, so the TA asked for numbers.
examples.zh: 我的「支撑细节」太空泛，助教让我引用具体数字。

words.enDefinition: the central point a paragraph or essay conveys

examples.en: Summarize the main idea of the article in one sentence first.
examples.zh: 先用一句话概括这篇文章的「主旨」。

examples.en: The tutor asked what the main idea of my second paragraph was.
examples.zh: 辅导老师问我第二段的「主旨」是什么。

collocations: the main idea of the paragraph

words.enDefinition: the central position the entire essay defends

examples.en: State your main argument in one sentence before you outline the paper.
examples.zh: 列提纲之前，先用一句话说出你的「核心论点」。

examples.en: My main argument got clearer after I cut the two side points.
examples.zh: 删掉两个次要论点之后，我的「核心论点」更清晰了。

words.enDefinition: the thesis repeated in fresh words at the end

examples.en: The restated thesis in my conclusion echoed the introduction too closely.
examples.zh: 我结论里的「重申论点」和开头呼应得太像了。

examples.en: A good restated thesis adds what the essay has now proven.
examples.zh: 好的「重申论点」要体现文章最终证明了什么。

collocations: a restated thesis in the conclusion

words.enDefinition: the overall arrangement of introduction, body, and conclusion

examples.en: Fix the essay structure first, then polish the individual sentences.
examples.zh: 先调整「文章结构」，再打磨单个句子。

examples.en: The rubric gives five points just for a clear essay structure.
examples.zh: 评分标准里，光是清晰的「文章结构」就占五分。

words.enDefinition: every sentence in a paragraph serving the same point

examples.en: Paragraph unity suffers when a sentence wanders off the main point.
examples.zh: 一旦有句子偏离主旨，「段落统一性」就被破坏了。

examples.en: The tutor deleted one sentence to restore my paragraph unity.
examples.zh: 辅导老师删掉一句，恢复了「段落统一性」。

words.enDefinition: the quality of ideas fitting together logically

examples.en: The TA praised the coherence of my argument across all five paragraphs.
examples.zh: 助教称赞我五个段落之间论证的「连贯性」。

examples.en: Read the draft aloud to check the coherence between your ideas.
examples.zh: 把草稿读出声，检查想法之间的「连贯性」。

collocations: the overall coherence of the essay

words.enDefinition: how sentences link smoothly through connectors and echoes

examples.en: My tutor showed how pronouns and linking phrases create cohesion between sentences.
examples.zh: 辅导老师示范了代词和连接语如何让句子之间产生「衔接」。

examples.en: The paragraph lacks cohesion because each sentence starts a new topic abruptly.
examples.zh: 这一段缺乏「衔接」，每句话都突兀地另起话题。

words.enDefinition: the smooth order in which points build on each other

examples.en: Reorder the middle sections to improve the logical flow of the paper.
examples.zh: 调整中间几节的顺序，改善文章的「逻辑连贯」。

examples.en: The writing tutor drew arrows to show where my logical flow broke down.
examples.zh: 写作辅导老师画箭头，标出我「逻辑连贯」中断的地方。

words.enDefinition: a point an opponent would raise against your position

examples.en: Address the strongest counterclaim in your fourth paragraph, then rebut it.
examples.zh: 在第四段处理最有力的「反方主张」，然后加以反驳。

examples.en: Ignoring the most obvious counterclaim made my whole essay look one-sided.
examples.zh: 无视最明显的「反方主张」，让我的整篇文章显得片面。

words.enDefinition: the section where you disprove opposing views

examples.en: My refutation quoted a recent study that contradicted the opposing view.
examples.zh: 我的「驳论」部分引用了一项与对方观点相矛盾的最新研究。

examples.en: A weak refutation just repeats your thesis instead of engaging the evidence.
examples.zh: 软弱无力的「驳论」只会重复论点，不正面回应证据。

words.enDefinition: admitting an opponent's point is partly valid before responding

examples.en: Concede a point about cost before arguing the policy is still worth it.
examples.zh: 在成本上「承认对方有理」，然后论证这项政策仍然值得。

examples.en: Strong essays concede a point to the other side before refuting it.
examples.zh: 高分的文章会先「承认对方有理」，再进行反驳。

collocations: be willing to concede a point

words.enDefinition: adding conditions that make a statement more defensible

examples.en: The TA showed me how to qualify a claim with words like generally or often.
examples.zh: 助教教我用 generally、often 这类词来「限定论点措辞」。

examples.en: Learning to qualify a claim will make your arguments much harder to attack.
examples.zh: 学会「限定论点措辞」，你的论证就更难被驳倒。

words.enDefinition: make a strong statement less absolute and more defensible

examples.en: Soften a claim like never by changing it to rarely.
examples.zh: 把 never 改成 rarely，就是「缓和论点措辞」。

examples.en: My tutor told me to soften the claim until the evidence could support it.
examples.zh: 辅导老师让我「缓和论点措辞」，直到证据撑得起为止。

collocations: soften a claim to match the evidence

words.enDefinition: a sweeping conclusion drawn from far too little evidence

examples.en: The TA marked my overgeneralization and asked for more representative examples.
examples.zh: 助教标出了我的「过度概括」，要求举更有代表性的例子。

examples.en: Calling all campuses unsafe from one survey is an overgeneralization.
examples.zh: 只凭一次调查就断言所有校园都不安全，是「过度概括」。

words.enDefinition: a short personal story illustrating a point

examples.en: Open with a one-sentence anecdote to make the issue feel real.
examples.zh: 开头用一个一句话的「小故事」，让议题显得真实。

examples.en: Her anecdote about her grandmother's hospital bills made the argument memorable.
examples.zh: 她讲的那段外婆医疗费的「轶事」让论证令人难忘。

collocations: use an anecdote as a hook

words.enDefinition: a number from research used as evidence

examples.en: Lead with a striking statistic, then explain what the number means.
examples.zh: 先用一个惊人的「统计数据」开头，再解释数字的含义。

examples.en: Never drop a statistic without naming where the figure came from.
examples.zh: 引用「统计数据」时，一定要说明数字的出处。

words.enDefinition: a specialist's judgment quoted to strengthen an argument

examples.en: Pair each expert opinion with data so the essay is not all quotes.
examples.zh: 每条「专家观点」都配上数据，文章就不会全是引文。

examples.en: My professor warned that expert opinion alone does not prove a claim.
examples.zh: 教授提醒我，光有「专家观点」并不能证明论点。

collocations: an expert opinion on the topic

words.enDefinition: give credit for borrowed ideas in a recognized format

examples.en: Whenever you cite a source, include the page number in parentheses.
examples.zh: 每次引用都要「注明引用来源」，并在括号里标出页码。

examples.en: Learn to cite sources properly before the first paper is due.
examples.zh: 第一篇论文截止之前，要学会规范地「标注引用来源」。

words.enDefinition: an essay that argues a position with reasons and evidence

examples.en: The final exam asks for an argumentative essay on campus housing policy.
examples.zh: 期末考试要求写一篇关于校园住房政策的「议论文」。

examples.en: An argumentative essay needs a debatable thesis, not a plain fact.
examples.zh: 「议论文」需要一个可争论的论点，而不是一个平铺的事实。

collocations: an argumentative essay on campus policy

words.enDefinition: an essay meant to convince readers to agree or act

examples.en: My persuasive essay ends with a call to action for students.
examples.zh: 我的「说服性文章」结尾呼吁学生们采取行动。

examples.en: Strong persuasive essays anticipate objections instead of simply ignoring them.
examples.zh: 高明的「说服性文章」会预判反对意见，而不是无视它们。

collocations: a persuasive essay for the class

words.enDefinition: an essay examining similarities and differences between subjects

examples.en: My compare and contrast essay examines two recycling programs side by side.
examples.zh: 我的「对比文章」把两个回收项目放在一起比较。

examples.en: Organize a compare and contrast essay by point, not by source.
examples.zh: 「对比文章」要按要点组织，而不是按来源组织。

collocations: write a compare and contrast essay
organize a compare and contrast essay by point
compare and contrast essay of two texts

words.enDefinition: an essay that explains a topic clearly with facts

examples.en: The expository essay explains the process without taking any side.
examples.zh: 「说明文」只解释过程，不表明立场。

examples.en: Use headings to keep your long expository essay easy to follow.
examples.zh: 给长篇「说明文」加小标题，读者更容易跟上。

collocations: an expository essay on a process

words.enDefinition: the serious, impersonal style academic writing expects

examples.en: Swap contractions for full forms to keep a formal tone throughout.
examples.zh: 把缩写形式换成完整写法，全文保持「正式语气」。

examples.en: The TA said my jokes broke the formal tone required by the assignment.
examples.zh: 助教说我的玩笑破坏了作业要求的「正式语气」。

words.enDefinition: careful wording like may or suggests that softens claims

examples.en: Use hedging language such as tends to when the evidence is mixed.
examples.zh: 证据不一致时，用「模糊限制语」，比如 tends to。

examples.en: Hedging language makes your conclusions sound cautious rather than overconfident.
examples.zh: 「模糊限制语」让结论显得谨慎，而不是过度自信。

collocations: hedging language like may and might

words.enDefinition: the measured, evidence-based style of college writing

examples.en: Finding your academic voice takes practice, especially in a second language.
examples.zh: 找到自己的「学术文风」需要练习，尤其是用第二语言写作时。

examples.en: My professor said my academic voice improved once I cut the slang.
examples.zh: 教授说删掉俚语之后，我的「学术文风」进步了。

words.enDefinition: the specific words picked to express each idea

examples.en: Awkward word choice made my otherwise strong paragraph hard to follow.
examples.zh: 别扭的「用词」让本来很强的段落变得难懂。

examples.en: The tutor suggested better word choices for three verbs in my abstract.
examples.zh: 辅导老师为摘要里的三个动词提出了更好的「用词」建议。

words.enDefinition: a writer's choice of words and style of expression

examples.en: The TA praised my diction in the conclusion as precise and varied.
examples.zh: 助教称赞我结论部分的「措辞」精准多变。

examples.en: Formal diction matters more in a research paper than in a blog.
examples.zh: 和博客相比，研究论文更讲究正式的「措辞」。

words.enDefinition: neutral writing that reports facts without personal feelings

examples.en: Keep an objective tone in the results, even if the data disappoints you.
examples.zh: 即使数据不理想，结果部分也要保持「客观语气」。

examples.en: My instructor asked for a more objective tone in the analysis section.
examples.zh: 老师要求分析部分用更「客观的语气」。

collocations: an objective tone in the analysis

words.enDefinition: casual style that feels out of place in academic work

examples.en: The TA flagged my informal tone, especially the contractions and jokes.
examples.zh: 助教标出了我的「非正式语气」，尤其是缩写和玩笑。

examples.en: Even your emails to professors should avoid a casual, informal tone.
examples.zh: 就连给教授的邮件，也避免随意、非正式的「语气」。

words.enDefinition: cautious wording like may or suggests that avoids absolutes

examples.en: Use tentative language, writing the data suggests instead of the data proves.
examples.zh: 用「委婉措辞」，写 the data suggests 而不是 the data proves。

examples.en: Tentative language keeps your conclusion open to future research questions.
examples.zh: 「委婉措辞」让你的结论为后续研究留出空间。

collocations: tentative language like may and might

words.enDefinition: saying the same idea or word too many times

examples.en: The TA circled the repetition of important in three consecutive sentences.
examples.zh: 助教圈出连续三句里反复出现的 important，指出「重复」问题。

examples.en: Some repetition is deliberate, but unintentional repetition weakens your prose.
examples.zh: 有些「重复」是有意为之，但无意的重复会削弱文笔。

words.enDefinition: mixing short and long sentences to keep prose lively

examples.en: Add sentence variety by combining some of those short choppy lines.
examples.zh: 把那些短促的句子合并一些，增加「句式多样性」。

examples.en: Sentence variety keeps readers engaged, so vary your openings deliberately.
examples.zh: 「句式多样性」能留住读者，所以要有意识地变换句首。

words.enDefinition: expressing ideas in the fewest clear words

examples.en: Trim the second paragraph until every line shows concise wording.
examples.zh: 精简第二段，让每一行都做到「简洁措辞」。

examples.en: The rubric rewards concise wording, so cut phrases that add nothing.
examples.zh: 评分标准看重「简洁措辞」，把没有实际内容的词组删掉。

words.enDefinition: using more words than the idea actually needs

examples.en: My instructor circled the wordiness in my introduction and said to tighten it.
examples.zh: 老师圈出我开头的「冗长啰嗦」，让我写得紧凑些。

examples.en: Wordiness often hides your point, especially in the first paragraph.
examples.zh: 「冗长啰嗦」常常掩盖你的观点，尤其是第一段。

words.enDefinition: special terms ordinary readers may not understand

examples.en: Define the jargon the first time each term appears in your paper.
examples.zh: 每个术语第一次在论文里出现时，都要先解释这个「行话」。

examples.en: Economics jargon confused my readers, so I added plain-language definitions.
examples.zh: 经济学「行话」让读者看不懂，我加了通俗的定义。

words.enDefinition: a casual spoken phrase that clashes with academic prose

examples.en: Replace every colloquial expression with a neutral academic equivalent in your draft.
examples.zh: 在草稿里，把每个「口语化表达」换成中性的学术说法。

examples.en: Kinda is a colloquial expression you should never use in an essay.
examples.zh: Kinda 这类「口语化表达」绝不该出现在论文里。

collocations: swap colloquial expressions for formal ones

words.enDefinition: a shortened form like don't that formal essays avoid

examples.en: Expand every contraction into its full form before you submit the final paper.
examples.zh: 提交终稿之前，把每个「缩写形式」都展开成完整形式。

examples.en: Contractions like it's and don't make research writing sound too casual.
examples.zh: it's 和 don't 这类「缩写形式」让研究性文章显得太随意。

words.enDefinition: an overused phrase that has lost its impact

examples.en: Since the dawn of time is a cliché that weakens any introduction.
examples.zh: Since the dawn of time 是削弱开头力度的「陈词滥调」。

examples.en: My tutor crossed out three cliches and told me to find fresher images.
examples.zh: 辅导老师划掉了三个「陈词滥调」，让我找更有新意的表达。

words.enDefinition: unnatural wording a native reader stumbles over

examples.en: The TA marked my awkward phrasing and rewrote one sentence as a model.
examples.zh: 助教标出我「别扭的表述」，并改写了一句作示范。

examples.en: Read your draft aloud; awkward phrasing usually signals a missing word.
examples.zh: 把草稿读出声，「别扭的表述」往往意味着漏了词。

collocations: awkward phrasing in the second paragraph

words.enDefinition: the quality of being easy for readers to follow

examples.en: Add examples wherever the TA's notes question the clarity of a point.
examples.zh: 凡是助教批注质疑「清晰度」的地方，都补上例子。

examples.en: Clarity improved a lot after I split that long sentence in two.
examples.zh: 把那个长句拆成两句后，「清晰度」提升了很多。

collocations: check the clarity of each paragraph

words.enDefinition: words like I and we that some instructors restrict

examples.en: This sociology course bans first-person pronouns, so write everything impersonally.
examples.zh: 这门社会学课禁用「第一人称代词」，所有句子都要写得客观。

examples.en: Overusing first-person pronouns made my analysis sound like a diary entry.
examples.zh: 过多使用「第一人称代词」让我的分析像日记。

collocations: replace first-person pronouns with the passive

words.enDefinition: writing about subjects without using I or you

examples.en: Rewrite the reflection in third person to match the course requirements.
examples.zh: 把这篇反思改用「第三人称」来写，以符合课程要求。

examples.en: Academic essays usually stay in third person unless the prompt says otherwise.
examples.zh: 学术文章一般通篇用「第三人称」，除非题目另有要求。

collocations: shift from first to third person

words.enDefinition: name the author before presenting their exact words

examples.en: Attribute a quote to its author the moment it appears in your paragraph.
examples.zh: 引文一出现，就要马上「注明引文出处」。

examples.en: Always attribute a quote correctly, because floating quotations confuse the reader.
examples.zh: 一定要正确「注明引文出处」，孤零零的引文会让读者困惑。

collocations: attribute a quote to its author
attribute quotes in a signal phrase

words.enDefinition: copy an author's exact words with no changes

examples.en: If you quote verbatim, every word and punctuation mark must match the original.
examples.zh: 如果「逐字引用」，每个词和标点都必须与原文完全一致。

examples.en: She decided to quote verbatim because paraphrasing would blur the definition.
examples.zh: 她决定「逐字引用」，因为换一种说法会模糊这个定义。

collocations: quote verbatim and cite the page

words.enDefinition: a verb like argues or notes introducing a source's view

examples.en: Choose a neutral reporting verb such as notes instead of proves.
examples.zh: 选择中性的「转述动词」，比如 notes，而不是 proves。

examples.en: Strong writers vary their reporting verbs to show each source's attitude.
examples.zh: 高水平的写作者会变换「转述动词」，体现各来源的态度。

collocations: reporting verbs like argues and notes

words.enDefinition: a short phrase that smoothly introduces a quotation

examples.en: Every quotation needs a lead-in so it does not drop in cold.
examples.zh: 每处引文都要有「引入语」，不能生硬地空降。

examples.en: My tutor showed me a lead-in that names the author and the context.
examples.zh: 辅导老师给我示范了一个点出作者和语境的「引入语」。

collocations: write a lead-in for each quotation

words.enDefinition: openly name where borrowed ideas or data came from

examples.en: Acknowledge the source right after each borrowed statistic or idea.
examples.zh: 每处借用的数据或观点，都要马上「注明资料出处」。

examples.en: Writers acknowledge the source even when they only borrow an outline.
examples.zh: 即使只借鉴了提纲，作者也要「注明资料出处」。

collocations: acknowledge the source of an idea

words.enDefinition: credit the original author for borrowed words or ideas

examples.en: Always give credit when an idea is not your own.
examples.zh: 只要想法不是你自己的，就要「注明出处」。

examples.en: Students who give credit properly rarely get accused of plagiarism.
examples.zh: 规范「注明出处」的学生，很少会被指抄袭。

collocations: give credit to the original author
give credit where it is due

words.enDefinition: format citations correctly according to the required style

examples.en: Learn to cite properly once, and every later paper gets easier.
examples.zh: 学会一次「规范引用」，以后每篇论文都会轻松些。

examples.en: The workshop taught first-year students how to cite properly in APA.
examples.zh: 工作坊教大一学生如何按 APA「规范引用」。

words.enDefinition: state a text's main points briefly and fairly

examples.en: Summarize a source in two sentences before you analyze it.
examples.zh: 在分析之前，先用两句话「概括文献要点」。

examples.en: My literature review summarizes each source, then groups them by theme.
examples.zh: 我的文献综述先「概括各篇文献」的要点，再按主题分组。

collocations: summarize a source in two sentences

words.enDefinition: one formatted line describing a single source

examples.en: Fix the indent on every reference list entry before submitting.
examples.zh: 提交前，把每条「参考文献条目」的缩进调好。

examples.en: Each reference list entry must match the borrowed text word for word.
examples.zh: 每条「参考文献条目」都要与所引文字一一对应。

words.enDefinition: a short note summarizing and evaluating a source

examples.en: Write a three-sentence annotation under each source in the bibliography list.
examples.zh: 在文献列表里，每条来源下面写三句话的「注释」。

examples.en: A good annotation summarizes the source and says why you will use it.
examples.zh: 好的「注释」既要概括来源，也要说明你为什么用它。

collocations: write an annotation for each source
summarize and evaluate in the annotation

words.enDefinition: a section surveying what researchers have already found

examples.en: The literature review showed a clear gap nobody has studied yet.
examples.zh: 「文献综述」显示出一个至今没人研究过的空白。

examples.en: Organize the literature review by theme instead of one study at a time.
examples.zh: 「文献综述」按主题组织，不要一篇一篇地罗列。

collocations: organize the literature review by theme

words.enDefinition: weighing a text's strengths and weaknesses rather than summarizing

examples.en: The assignment needs critical analysis, not just a summary of each article.
examples.zh: 这次作业需要「批判性分析」，而不只是概括每篇文章。

examples.en: Her critical analysis questioned the sample behind the famous study.
examples.zh: 她的「批判性分析」质疑了那项著名研究的样本。

collocations: offer a critical analysis of the source

words.enDefinition: the established theory your analysis leans on

examples.en: State your theoretical framework in one paragraph before the methods section.
examples.zh: 在方法部分之前，用一段话说明你的「理论框架」。

examples.en: Her theoretical framework draws on motivation research from the 1980s.
examples.zh: 她的「理论框架」借鉴了二十世纪八十年代的动机研究。

collocations: ground the analysis in a theoretical framework

words.enDefinition: the part of a paper explaining how data was collected

examples.en: The methods section should let another student repeat your study exactly.
examples.zh: 「方法部分」要让别的同学能完全重复你的研究。

examples.en: My TA asked for more detail about interviews in the methods section.
examples.zh: 助教要求「方法部分」把访谈过程写得更详细。

collocations: the methods section describes the sample

words.enDefinition: an honest weakness admitted in a study

examples.en: Mention the small sample as a study limitation in your final paragraph.
examples.zh: 在结尾段把样本过小列为「研究局限」。

examples.en: Every study limitation you admit makes the rest of your claims stronger.
examples.zh: 你承认的每个「研究局限」都会让其余论点更可信。

words.enDefinition: combine several studies into one connected discussion

examples.en: Group the studies by theme so you can synthesize sources instead of listing them.
examples.zh: 按主题给研究分组，这样才能「综合文献」，而不是逐篇罗列。

examples.en: A strong literature review will synthesize sources with opposite conclusions.
examples.zh: 高水平的文献综述会「综合文献」，哪怕它们结论相反。

words.enDefinition: a short summary of a paper placed before the introduction

examples.en: Write the abstract last, once the final numbers are in.
examples.zh: 等所有数据敲定之后，再写「摘要」。

examples.en: The abstract must state the purpose, method, and key result in 150 words.
examples.zh: 「摘要」要用一百五十词说清目的、方法和主要结果。

words.enDefinition: a handful of terms helping searchers find the paper

examples.en: List about five keywords under the abstract, separated by semicolons.
examples.zh: 在摘要下方列出五个左右的「关键词」，用分号隔开。

examples.en: Choose keywords readers would actually type into the library database.
examples.zh: 选的「关键词」要贴近读者在图书馆数据库里真正会输入的词。

words.enDefinition: a small margin box holding a reviewer's note

examples.en: Click each comment bubble before revising so no suggestion gets lost.
examples.zh: 修改前把每个「批注气泡」点开看，别漏掉任何建议。

examples.en: There is a comment bubble on paragraph three asking for evidence.
examples.zh: 第三段有个「批注气泡」，要求补充论据。

collocations: a comment bubble in the margin

words.enDefinition: a written note placed in the page's margin

examples.en: Her margin comment asked me to define the term on first use.
examples.zh: 她的「页边批注」让我在术语首次出现时给出定义。

examples.en: I answered every margin comment in a different color before resubmitting.
examples.zh: 重交之前，我用另一种颜色逐条回复了「页边批注」。

words.enDefinition: a note anchored directly inside the text

examples.en: She left an inline comment right where the missing citation belongs.
examples.zh: 她就在缺引用的位置留了一条「行内批注」。

examples.en: Reply to each inline comment so your professor sees your changes.
examples.zh: 每条「行内批注」都要回复，让教授看到你的修改。

collocations: an inline comment on the sentence

words.enDefinition: mark a reviewer's note as addressed and close it

examples.en: Resolve a comment only after you have actually fixed the issue.
examples.zh: 真正把问题改好之后，再「解决批注」。

examples.en: The tutor said to never resolve a comment before checking the fix.
examples.zh: 辅导老师说，确认修改有效之前不要「解决批注」。

collocations: resolve the comment after fixing it

words.enDefinition: a proposed change shown for you to accept or reject

examples.en: Accept each suggested edit only if you understand why it improves the sentence.
examples.zh: 只有明白每条「建议修改」为什么更好，才去点接受。

examples.en: The tutor left a suggested edit turning my passive sentence into active voice.
examples.zh: 辅导老师留了一条「建议修改」，把我的被动句改成了主动语态。

collocations: a suggested edit in suggest mode

words.enDefinition: the Google Docs setting that proposes edits without applying them

examples.en: Share the draft in suggest mode so I can propose edits directly.
examples.zh: 用「建议模式」共享草稿，这样我能直接提出修改建议。

examples.en: In suggest mode, every change I type shows up as a colored suggestion.
examples.zh: 在「建议模式」下，我打的每处改动都会显示成彩色建议。

collocations: share the doc in suggest mode
switch from suggest mode to editing

words.enDefinition: approve one proposed edit in a reviewed document

examples.en: Accept a change by right-clicking the highlighted text in Word.
examples.zh: 在 Word 里右键点高亮文字就能「接受修订」。

examples.en: I accept a change only when it truly improves the sentence.
examples.zh: 只有真正改进句子的修订，我才会「接受修订」。

collocations: accept a change one by one

words.enDefinition: turn down a proposed edit and keep your wording

examples.en: You can reject a change if the edit distorts your original point.
examples.zh: 如果修订扭曲了你原本的意思，可以「拒绝修订」。

examples.en: My editor kept my meaning intact, so I chose not to reject a change.
examples.zh: 编辑完全保留了原意，所以我没有「拒绝修订」任何一处。

collocations: reject a change and explain why

words.enDefinition: a tool flagging possibly misspelled words

examples.en: Run the spell checker, but remember it misses correctly spelled wrong words.
examples.zh: 跑一遍「拼写检查器」，但注意它查不出拼写正确却用错的词。

examples.en: The spell checker flagged ten words, and three were actually fine.
examples.zh: 「拼写检查器」标出了十个词，其中三个其实没有错。

words.enDefinition: software that spots grammar and style problems

examples.en: A grammar checker catches comma splices that spell check misses.
examples.zh: 「语法检查器」能查出拼写检查漏掉的逗号粘连。

examples.en: Do not trust the grammar checker blindly; it often flags correct passive voice.
examples.zh: 别盲信「语法检查器」，它经常把正确的被动语态标成错误。

collocations: the grammar checker flags style issues

words.enDefinition: a sentence mistake such as wrong tense or agreement

examples.en: The TA fixed one grammar error per page instead of correcting everything.
examples.zh: 助教每页只改一处「语法错误」，而不是全部代改。

examples.en: Most of my grammar errors came from translating Chinese structures directly.
examples.zh: 我的「语法错误」大多来自直接套用中文结构。

collocations: a grammar error in every paragraph

words.enDefinition: a wrong or missing mark such as a misplaced comma

examples.en: Most of my punctuation errors were missing commas after introductory phrases.
examples.zh: 我的「标点错误」大多是在句首短语后漏了逗号。

examples.en: The rubric deducts half a point for each repeated punctuation error.
examples.zh: 评分标准对重复出现的「标点错误」每次扣半分。

words.enDefinition: text shown with a line through it to mark deletion

examples.en: The tutor used strikethrough to show exactly which clause to cut.
examples.zh: 辅导老师用「删除线」标出到底要删哪个从句。

examples.en: Keep the strikethrough text visible so I can see what you removed.
examples.zh: 保留「删除线」文字，让我看到你删了什么。

words.enDefinition: one focused revision of a draft for a single issue

examples.en: Do one editing pass just for commas, then another for word choice.
examples.zh: 先做一轮只看逗号的「修改轮次」，再做一轮只看用词的。

examples.en: My final editing pass focused on citations because content was already solid.
examples.zh: 最后一轮「修改轮次」我只核对引用，因为内容已经稳定。

words.enDefinition: one complete careful reading right before submission

examples.en: Print the essay and do a slow final read-through away from the screen.
examples.zh: 把文章打印出来，离开屏幕慢慢做一次「最后通读」。

examples.en: During the final read-through, I caught two paragraphs that repeated each other.
examples.zh: 「最后通读」时我发现了两段互相重复的内容。

words.enDefinition: an outline made after drafting by summarizing each paragraph

examples.en: Make a reverse outline by writing one line per existing paragraph.
examples.zh: 给已有的每段各写一句话，就做成了一份「反向提纲」。

examples.en: My reverse outline revealed that paragraphs four and five argue the same point.
examples.zh: 「反向提纲」暴露出第四、五两段其实在论证同一个观点。

collocations: a reverse outline of the draft
use a reverse outline to reorganize

words.enDefinition: a construction where the subject receives the action

examples.en: The TA circled the passive voice and asked who actually performed the action.
examples.zh: 助教圈出「被动语态」，问到底是谁做的动作。

examples.en: Passive voice is fine in methods sections, where the actor does not matter.
examples.zh: 方法部分用「被动语态」没问题，因为动作执行者并不重要。

collocations: the passive voice in scientific writing

words.enDefinition: a construction where the subject performs the action

examples.en: Rewrite the sentence in active voice to name the responsible researcher.
examples.zh: 把这句改成「主动语态」，点出到底是哪位研究者做的。

examples.en: Active voice usually needs fewer words than the passive version.
examples.zh: 「主动语态」通常比被动说法用词更少。

words.enDefinition: two or more sentences joined without proper punctuation

examples.en: The first sentence of your essay is a run-on sentence; split it in two.
examples.zh: 你文章的第一句是个「连写句」，把它拆成两句吧。

examples.en: My tutor found three run-on sentences in the opening paragraph alone.
examples.zh: 光是开头段，辅导老师就找出了三个「连写句」。

words.enDefinition: the error of joining two full sentences with only a comma

examples.en: The comma splice in line four is easy to fix with a semicolon.
examples.zh: 第四行的「逗号粘连」用一个分号就能轻松解决。

examples.en: A comma splice happens when you join two independent clauses with just a comma.
examples.zh: 只用逗号连接两个独立分句，就会造成「逗号粘连」。

collocations: fix the comma splice with a semicolon

words.enDefinition: a word group punctuated as a sentence but missing parts

examples.en: That four-word sentence fragment works fine for emphasis in a hook.
examples.zh: 这个四词的「句子残缺」放在引子里反而有强调效果。

examples.en: Every sentence fragment in my draft came from forgetting the subject.
examples.zh: 我草稿里的每个「句子残缺」都是因为漏了主语。

words.enDefinition: matching a verb's form to its subject's number

examples.en: Subject-verb agreement slips like the data shows confuse careful readers.
examples.zh: 像 the data shows 这样的「主谓一致」失误会让认真的读者分心。

examples.en: Long sentences are where subject-verb agreement errors hide most often.
examples.zh: 「主谓一致」的错误最常藏在长句里。

words.enDefinition: a describing phrase attached to the wrong subject

examples.en: The dangling modifier in line two makes it sound like the data walked home.
examples.zh: 第二行的「垂悬修饰语」读起来好像数据自己走回了家。

examples.en: Fix the dangling modifier by naming who actually did the reading.
examples.zh: 修掉这个「垂悬修饰语」，写清楚到底是谁在读那本书。

words.enDefinition: a descriptive word placed next to the wrong noun

examples.en: A misplaced modifier like only drifting from its word changes the whole meaning.
examples.zh: 「错位修饰语」的典型情况是 only 远离了它限定的词。

examples.en: The misplaced modifier made the sentence describe the dog instead of the student.
examples.zh: 这个「错位修饰语」让句子描写了狗，而不是那个学生。

words.enDefinition: repeating the same grammatical pattern across a list

examples.en: Keep parallel structure in that list by making every item a gerund.
examples.zh: 让列表里每一项都用动名词，保持「平行结构」。

examples.en: The thesis reads better once the three clauses follow parallel structure.
examples.zh: 三个从句都遵循「平行结构」之后，论点句读起来顺畅多了。

collocations: a parallel structure of three clauses

words.enDefinition: a punctuation mark joining two closely related full sentences

examples.en: Use a semicolon to join those two sentences instead of a comma.
examples.zh: 用「分号」连接那两个句子，别只用逗号。

examples.en: A semicolon before however fixes the splice without adding words.
examples.zh: 在 however 前加一个「分号」，不用增词就能解决粘连。

collocations: join two sentences with a semicolon

words.enDefinition: a word group able to stand alone as a sentence

examples.en: Every independent clause needs its own subject and a complete verb.
examples.zh: 每个「独立分句」都要有自己的主语和完整的动词。

examples.en: Join two independent clauses with a semicolon or a comma plus a conjunction.
examples.zh: 两个「独立分句」之间要用分号，或用逗号加连词连接。

collocations: an independent clause and a dependent clause

words.enDefinition: a clause starting with although or because that cannot stand alone

examples.en: A dependent clause starting with because cannot stand by itself.
examples.zh: 以 because 开头的「从属分句」不能单独成句。

examples.en: Put a comma after the dependent clause when it opens the sentence.
examples.zh: 「从属分句」放在句首时，后面要加逗号。

collocations: a dependent clause at the start
a comma after the dependent clause

words.enDefinition: the time form of a verb, like past or present

examples.en: Check every verb tense when you describe what a study did.
examples.zh: 描述某项研究做了什么时，逐个核对「动词时态」。

examples.en: Shifting verb tense mid-paragraph is one of the most common mistakes.
examples.zh: 段落中间「动词时态」乱切换，是最常见的错误之一。

words.enDefinition: a pronoun whose antecedent is unclear to the reader

examples.en: The vague pronoun it could refer to the theory or the experiment.
examples.zh: 这个「指代不明」的 it，可能指理论，也可能指实验。

examples.en: Fix vague pronouns by naming the noun instead of saying this.
examples.zh: 修掉「指代不明」，直接写出名词，别只说 this。

collocations: a vague pronoun like it or this

words.enDefinition: the mark showing possession or missing letters

examples.en: Check each apostrophe carefully; students often confuse its and it's.
examples.zh: 逐个检查「撇号」，同学们经常把 its 和 it's 混淆。

examples.en: A missing apostrophe turned student's essay into students essay in my draft.
examples.zh: 漏写一个「撇号」，草稿里的 student's essay 就变成了 students essay。

words.enDefinition: marks like commas and periods that organize sentences

examples.en: Read for punctuation before you submit; missing commas confuse readers.
examples.zh: 提交前专门检查「标点符号」，漏掉的逗号会让读者困惑。

examples.en: Good punctuation alone will not save a weak or confusing argument.
examples.zh: 就算「标点符号」全对，也救不了软弱混乱的论证。

words.enDefinition: a joining word like and, but, or so

examples.en: Add a coordinating conjunction like but to fix that comma splice.
examples.zh: 加一个 but 这样的「并列连词」，就能修好那个逗号粘连。

examples.en: Two independent clauses need a coordinating conjunction or a semicolon between them.
examples.zh: 两个独立分句之间要有「并列连词」，或者用分号。

collocations: join clauses with a coordinating conjunction

words.enDefinition: the campus service offering free help with any writing

examples.en: Book a session at the writing center before the midterm essay is due.
examples.zh: 期中论文截止前，先在「写作中心」预约一次辅导。

examples.en: The writing center tutors will not edit for you, but they will teach you.
examples.zh: 「写作中心」的辅导老师不会替你改，但会教你方法。

collocations: book a session at the writing center
the writing center on the second floor

words.enDefinition: a scheduled one-on-one session with a writing tutor

examples.en: My writing center appointment is Thursday at three, right after linguistics.
examples.zh: 我的「写作中心预约」在周四三点，刚好排在语言学课后。

examples.en: Cancel the writing center appointment online if you cannot make it.
examples.zh: 如果去不了，就在网上取消「写作中心预约」。

words.enDefinition: an open time period you can reserve online

examples.en: The writing center's appointment slots for next week open Monday morning.
examples.zh: 写作中心下周的「预约时段」周一早上开放。

examples.en: Grab an early appointment slot before tutors are fully booked.
examples.zh: 趁辅导老师还没约满，赶紧抢一个早上的「预约时段」。

words.enDefinition: a trained student or staff member coaching your writing

examples.en: The writing tutor asked me to read my paragraph aloud first.
examples.zh: 「写作辅导老师」让我先把那个段落读出声。

examples.en: Ask the writing tutor for a plan instead of a quick fix.
examples.zh: 让「写作辅导老师」给你一套方法，而不是临时打补丁。

words.enDefinition: a scheduled meeting focused on your draft

examples.en: Bring two printed copies to every tutoring session, one for the tutor.
examples.zh: 每次去「辅导课」都带两份打印稿，一份给老师。

examples.en: My tutoring session starts with five minutes of goal setting.
examples.zh: 我的「辅导课」开头五分钟先定这次的目标。

collocations: come prepared to the tutoring session
start the tutoring session with goals

words.enDefinition: walk-in writing help needing no advance booking

examples.en: Drop-in sessions fill fast during finals week, so arrive early.
examples.zh: 期末周「免预约辅导」很快就满了，所以要早点去。

examples.en: Use a short drop-in session for quick questions about citations.
examples.zh: 用简短的「免预约辅导」解决引用方面的小问题。

collocations: no appointment needed for drop-in sessions

words.enDefinition: a short printed guide covering one writing topic

examples.en: The writing handout on integrating quotations fits on one page.
examples.zh: 那份讲引用融合的「写作讲义」只有一页。

examples.en: Grab the free writing handout about thesis statements near the front desk.
examples.zh: 在前台旁边取一份讲论点句的免费「写作讲义」。

words.enDefinition: rework a draft's ideas and structure after feedback

examples.en: Revise the introduction first because it sets up everything after it.
examples.zh: 先「修改」引言，因为它决定了后面的一切。

examples.en: After the TA meeting, I revised my outline before touching the draft.
examples.zh: 和助教谈完之后，我先「修改」了提纲，再动草稿。

words.enDefinition: add explanation and evidence to a thin paragraph

examples.en: Expand a paragraph whenever the TA marks it as too thin.
examples.zh: 凡是助教标注太单薄的段落，都要「扩写段落」。

examples.en: Expand a paragraph by explaining the quote, not just dropping it in.
examples.zh: 「扩写段落」时要解释引文，而不是把引文丢在那儿。

collocations: expand a paragraph with a source

words.enDefinition: cut extra words until only the point remains

examples.en: Trim a paragraph by deleting any sentence that repeats the first point.
examples.zh: 删掉重复第一个观点的句子，把段落「精简」一下。

examples.en: When the essay runs long, trim a paragraph instead of cutting the whole section.
examples.zh: 文章超长时，逐段「精简」，而不是整节删掉。

collocations: trim a paragraph by one sentence

words.enDefinition: remove weak points so the case builds sharply

examples.en: Cut the tangent about social media; it does not tighten the argument.
examples.zh: 删掉社交媒体那段题外话，它无助于「收紧论证」。

examples.en: Tighten the argument by making each paragraph serve the thesis directly.
examples.zh: 让每一段都直接服务论点，从而「收紧论证」。

collocations: tighten the argument by cutting tangents
tighten the argument in the middle

words.enDefinition: develop reasons and evidence into a convincing case

examples.en: Build an argument one claim at a time, evidence first, then analysis.
examples.zh: 一条主张一条主张地「展开论证」，先证据后分析。

examples.en: It is easier to build an argument after you narrow the topic.
examples.zh: 先缩小题目范围，再「展开论证」会容易得多。

words.enDefinition: back a statement with evidence or reasoning

examples.en: One statistic is not enough to support a claim this broad.
examples.zh: 一条统计数据不足以「支撑论点」，这条论点太宽泛了。

examples.en: Quote the interview directly when you support a claim about student stress.
examples.zh: 想要「支撑论点」，就直接引用访谈里关于学生压力的原话。

collocations: support each claim with a citation

words.enDefinition: focus a broad subject into something manageable

examples.en: Narrow the topic from social media to one app's effect on sleep.
examples.zh: 先「缩小题目范围」，从社交媒体聚焦到某款应用对睡眠的影响。

examples.en: My professor told me to narrow the topic or the paper would sprawl.
examples.zh: 教授让我「缩小题目范围」，否则论文会写得太散。

collocations: narrow the topic to one question

words.enDefinition: keep every paragraph tied to the main question

examples.en: Every paragraph must stay on topic and serve the research question.
examples.zh: 每一段都要「紧扣主题」，服务于研究问题。

examples.en: Long essays drift easily, so keep reminding yourself to stay on topic.
examples.zh: 长文容易写散，要不断提醒自己「不跑题」。

collocations: stay on topic in every paragraph

words.enDefinition: wander away from the main subject while writing

examples.en: My conclusion digressed into university policy and had to be rewritten.
examples.zh: 我的结论「跑题」扯到了学校政策上，只好重写。

examples.en: The tutor marked the paragraph where I digress from pricing to packaging.
examples.zh: 辅导老师标出了我从定价「跑题」到包装的那一段。

collocations: easy to digress in long essays

words.enDefinition: answer exactly what the assignment question asks

examples.en: Reread the assignment sheet to make sure your thesis addresses the prompt.
examples.zh: 重读作业说明，确认论点「紧扣题目要求」。

examples.en: Half the class lost points for essays that never addressed the prompt.
examples.zh: 一半同学因为文章没有「紧扣题目要求」而丢了分。

collocations: address every part of the prompt

words.enDefinition: writing nonstop for a few minutes to unlock ideas

examples.en: Try ten minutes of freewriting before you look at any sources.
examples.zh: 看任何文献之前，先做十分钟「自由写作」。

examples.en: Freewriting helped me discover what I actually think about the article.
examples.zh: 「自由写作」帮我看清了自己对这篇文章的真实想法。
